title: Position Management
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/0/title: Where the idea is proven wrong
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/0/body: A sensible stop loss sits where, if price gets there, **the trade idea is invalid**. For a buy that's usually **just below the last swing low**, and for a sell **just above the last swing high**, because breaking it means the trend structure has changed.
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/1/body: Leave a **small buffer** below the low (a few pips or a fraction of the **ATR**, the average true range) so a normal wick doesn't take out your stop. A wider stop means a **smaller position**: your dollar risk should stay the same.
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/2/prompt: You sold in this downtrend. Tap the candle whose high your stop should sit just above (the last swing high).
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/2/explanation: This candle's high is above the two candles before and after it, and it's the downtrend's last lower high (LH). If price goes above it, the bearish structure is broken and the sell idea is invalid.
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/3/prompt: You bought at 1.2745. Which line is the more sensible stop loss?
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/3/explanation: B is just below the last swing low (1.2700), where a break would invalidate the idea. A sits inside the last candle's normal range and gets hit by an ordinary wick. C is far away for no reason and only shrinks your allowed size.
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/4/prompt: Your account is $20,000 and you risk 1%. Your stop behind the swing on EUR/USD is 80 pips away. What's the right size in lots?
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/4/explanation: 200 ÷ (80 × 10) = 0.25 lots. At this size, if your stop gets hit you lose exactly $200, which is 1% of the account.
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/5/statement: If your stop behind the swing is further away, you should cut your position size so your dollar risk stays the same.
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/5/explanation: The chart structure decides where your stop goes, and your plan decides your dollar risk. Position size is the only variable you adjust to fit the stop distance.
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/6/sentence: Put the stop on a buy just ___ the last swing low, because breaking it means the ___ structure is gone.
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/6/explanation: In an uptrend, higher lows are the backbone of the structure. If the last low breaks, there's no reason to stay in the buy.
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/7/prompt: Why don't traders put their stop exactly on the swing low, with no buffer at all?
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/7/options/0: Price often wicks just below obvious lows and then comes back
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/7/options/2: Swing lows don't matter at all
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/7/options/3: A stop loss always has to be 100 pips
lessons/swing-u3-l1/steps/7/explanation: Lots of stop losses pile up right below obvious lows, and price sometimes tags them for a moment and comes back. A small buffer lowers the chance of getting shaken out by that noise.
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/0/body: A **trailing stop** means moving your stop loss **in the direction of profit**. In swing trading, the most common way is this: after each new high, once a **fresh swing low (HL)** forms, move your stop below it.
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/1/body: Instead of closing your whole position at one point, you can close **part of it** at the first target (like **1R** or the first resistance) and trail the rest. Many traders move the stop on the rest to **entry (breakeven)** after the first exit.
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/2/prompt: Price made a new high and a fresh swing low too. Using the swing trailing method, where do you move your stop?
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/2/options/0/la: A: just below the new swing low
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/2/options/1/la: B: right below the current price
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/2/options/2/la: C: leave it where it was
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/2/explanation: The new low (around 61,200) is above the previous low, so the stop goes below it. B sits inside normal swings and gets hit by the first pullback. C doesn't lock in any profit.
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/3/prompt: You bought 2 lots of GBP/USD at 1.2700. You closed 1 lot at 1.2760 and moved the second lot's stop to entry. Then price turned, and the second lot closed at breakeven. What's your total profit?
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/3/explanation: First lot: 60 pips × $10 = $600. The second lot closed at breakeven: zero. Total $600, on a trade that could have ended with nothing without a partial exit.
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/4/statement: You should never move your stop further from price, against the direction of profit.
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/4/explanation: Moving your stop further away means raising the risk you accepted at the start, right when the trade is going against you. Trailing only goes one way: in the direction of profit.
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/5/prompt: Put the steps of managing a swing buy with a trailing stop in order.
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/5/items/0: Enter with a stop below the swing low
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/5/items/3: Move your stop below the new low
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/5/explanation: The stop only moves once the new structure (a higher high, then a higher low) is complete, not on every green candle.
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/6/prompt: What's the biggest benefit of partial exits?
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/6/options/0: Part of the profit is locked in, and the rest can catch a big move
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/6/options/1: It always increases your total profit
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/6/options/2: It removes the need for a stop loss
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/6/options/3: It pushes your win rate to 100%
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/6/explanation: Partial exits are a trade-off: if price runs straight to the final target, you make less than holding the full size. But on reversals, part of the profit is safe, and there's less mental pressure too.
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/7/pairs/0/mean: Moving the stop in the direction of profit
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/7/pairs/1/mean: Stop loss at the entry price
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/7/pairs/2/mean: Closing part of the position at each target
lessons/swing-u3-l2/steps/7/pairs/3/mean: A profit equal to your initial risk
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/0/body: Forex closes Friday night and reopens around Sunday night (London time) as Asia opens. If big news breaks over the weekend, price can open with a **gap**, and your stop loss can fill at a **worse price** than the one you set.
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/1/prompt: Tap the candle that opened with a gap after the weekend.
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/1/explanation: Every candle opened right at the previous candle's close, except this one. It opened much higher, leaving an empty space between it and the previous candle. That's the start-of-week gap.
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/2/prompt: You bought 1 lot of EUR/USD at 1.0850 with a stop at 1.0800 ($500 risk). On Monday the market gapped open at 1.0770. What happens?
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/2/options/0: The stop fills around 1.0770: a loss of about $800
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/2/options/1: The stop fills exactly at 1.0800: a $500 loss
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/2/options/2: The stop fills around 1.0770: a loss of about $300
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/2/options/3: The stop doesn't fill, so there's no loss
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/2/explanation: Price never traded at 1.0800, so the stop fills at the first available price, around 1.0770. 80 pips × $10 = about $800, 60% more than the risk you planned.
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/3/statement: A stop loss always fills exactly at the price you set, even if the market gaps open.
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/3/explanation: Once triggered, a regular stop loss closes at the first available price, and in a gap that price can be much worse. Some brokers offer guaranteed stop losses for an extra fee.
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/4/body: Review your positions before the weekend: some swing traders **cut their size**, **take some profit** or **stay out** entirely before big events (like elections). Crypto trades on weekends too, but **thinner liquidity** can cause sharp moves.
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/5/prompt: Put a swing trader's Friday evening checklist in order.
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/5/items/0: Check the calendar for weekend events
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/5/items/1: Review open positions and their total risk
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/5/items/2: Work out the worst case, assuming a gap
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/5/items/3: If it's too much, cut size or take profit
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/5/explanation: First you find out what risks the weekend holds, then how exposed you are. You size up the worst case assuming a gap, and only cut risk if it's more than you can handle.
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/6/prompt: It's Friday. You have a GBP/USD buy that's 2R in profit, and a major UK election is happening over the weekend. What's the most sensible move?
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/6/options/0: Take some profit and move the stop on the rest into profit
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/6/options/1: Double your size because the trend is up
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/6/options/2: Remove your stop so a gap can't close it
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/6/options/3: Do nothing; gaps always open in the trend's direction
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/6/explanation: A big weekend event makes a gap more likely. Locking in some profit and moving your stop into profit limits the worst case, though in a sharp gap even your stop may fill with slippage.
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/7/sentence: The distance between Friday's closing price and the next week's opening price is called a ___.
lessons/swing-u3-l3/steps/7/explanation: No trades happen while the market is closed. If conditions have changed, the first price of the new week starts some distance away from Friday's price.
